campaigns/campaign-1/locations/zephyros/.description:
The campaign begins in Zephyros, with characters starting at level 3. Your character may be a resident of Zephyros or a visitor, but they must have a reason to currently be in the city.A recently exposed crime lord named Mathias Malnor is scheduled to be publicly executed. Public executions are rare in Zephyros and are generally reserved for people whose crimes have affected the city as a whole. Your character should have a reason to attend the execution or be nearby when it occurs. The characters do not need to know one another before the campaign begins but they can if that interests anyone.Y'all know how to write backstories but when writing your backstory, establish: Why your character is currently in Zephyros. Whether they live in the city and, if so, which district they come from. Who in the city do they know What is the character trying to accomplish One reason they would be willing to work with others when something dangerous happens. The Eye of Zephyros: The city’s primary police and investigative organization.
The Hand of Zephyros: Zephyros’ military, security, and intelligence organization.
The Will of Zephyros: The judicial body responsible for courts, trials, and legal judgments. City Summary Zephyros is a heavily influential city-state located on the eastern coast of the Sea of Silver. It is best known for its World's Wonder Market, a market open year-round where people from all over eastern Alteres, from master craftsmen to amateur hobbyists, gather to sell their goods. Castle Winterlow lies outside its walls atop Mt. Tempest.





Location: The Eastern Coast of the Sea of Silver, on the continent of Alteres City Type: City-State Approximate Population: ~126,000 30% Human 15% Elf 15% Dwarf 10% Gnome 10% Halfling 5% Half-Elf 5% Tiefling 2% Orc 8% Other Demonym: Zephyrian Government: Monarchy
Ruler(s): Vox Winterlow – King of Zephyros Primary Languages: Common, Alteran, Elvish, Dwarven Commercial Capital of Eastern Alteres Port City – !!!VERY IMPORTANT!!!
World's Wonder Market
Winterlow Trials Tone: Cosmopolitan, Prosperous Visual Inspiration: German & Baroque Architecture Cultural Inspiration: Comparable to Waterdeep/Neverwinter Copper Pieces: Copper Pieces Silver Pieces: Silver Pieces Gold Pieces: Suns Platinum Pieces: Moons Things all citizens know: There is a single bridge connecting Northern and Southern Zephyros.
The Winterlows came into power after the Zephyrian Revolution (circa 32 PE)
Zephyros owes much of its wealth to its ports and the World's Wonder Market, serving as a commercial hub for merchants across Eastern Alteres.
Zephyros operates on a legal code which is enforced by three primary groups: the Eye of Zephyros, the Hand of Zephyros, and the Will of Zephyros.
Every other year, the city gathers for the Winterlow Trials, a dangerous gauntlet of games and challenges.
People who compete in the Winterlow Trials are held in extremely high regard; the victor is awarded a monetary prize and residence in a mansion in the Gilded Quay until the next trial. Surrounding Terrain: surrounded by plains of grass, with roads connecting it to nearby cities and towns. To the north, there is a vast expanse of forest; to the west is the Sea of Silver. Natural Features: The Silver River runs through the city
Mt. Tempest to the north– With Castle Winterlow at its peak
Defenses: Hand of Zephyros, Wardens Primary Entrances: 1 gate to the North; 2 gate to the South; 2 gates to the East Common Transportation: Rental transportation (Horse, Oxen, Griffon) Purpose: The Government Center hosts most of Zephyros' government buildings. While the castle lies outside the city walls, the King and those who serve the monarchy visit the Government Center to take care of the city and appeal to citizens' requests. Appearance: Unlike the German/Baroque architecture common in zephyros, the Government Center style mostly resembles Greco-Roman architecture. Sandstone buildings dominate the Government Center. Intricate carvings of past royalty hold pillars of the larger structures with the motif of a meander lining the trim of most buildings Who Lives or Works Here: The majority of workers are monarchy officials, clerks, and civil servants. Besides government buildings, certain shops that are backed/sponsored by the monarchy are set up in the center.Purpose: Residential area for the upper class citizens of Zephyros. Its close proximity to Castle Winterlow and distance from the dense commercial districts makes property here some of the most valuable in the city. Residences vary from single-family houses to large apartments. Appearance: Well-maintained streets running between half-timbered townhouses, enclosed gardens, and larger private estates. Visually, the architecture in the High District is German, with little Baroque, inspiration. Who Lives or Works Here: Noble families and other highly successful citizen, such as merchants, tradesmen, and retired government officials, live here.Purpose: The Squall Ward provides inexpensive housing and services for northern Zephyros and houses much of the working class. The district also contains inexpensive inns, workshops, taverns, and neighborhood shops. Appearance: Streets in the Squall Ward are narrow with buildings crowding in and irregular streets. Buildings here are mostly old plaster and weathered timber with patched roofs. Some buildings have new additions attached that are visibly newer. Strong winds and sea spray weather the buildings nearer to the waterfront faster than those more inland. Who Lives or Works Here: Dockworkers, fishers, sailors, laborers, small-scale merchants, and poorer families. Purpose: The Port District manages most of the cities port duties. Cargo arriving by sea is unloaded here before being distributed to the rest of the city. Appearance: The waterfront is lined with many ports, piers, warehouses, shipyards, and customs offices. The main roads in the Port District are wide allowing for carts to travel on both sides. Closer to the docks, the sides of roads are often occupied with carts, cargo, and temporary stalls. Who Lives or Works Here: Dockworkers, managers, sailors, and merchants. Many inns and taverns are here to serve the regulars of the districtPurpose: The Trade District draws merchants, traders, and master craftsmen from all eastern Alteres to the city. The district is famous for the high commercial success of shop keepers who sell here. Appearance: The Trade District surrounds a central marketplace, with wide and stone brick paved roads. Permanent shops occupy the bottom floors of buildings with temporary stalls lining along the roads. The shops in this district sell a diverse expanse of specialized goods. Who Lives or Works Here: The majority of buildings in the Trade Ward are markets, inns, or taverns. Some shop owners live in residences above or below their stores.Purpose: The Bridge Ward surrounds the southern approach to the only bridge connecting northern and southern Zephyros. It serves travelers, transports goods between both halves of the city, and acts as a meeting point between several districts. Appearance: The streets of the Bridge Ward are dense and heavily traveled, with major roads converging near the bridge. Coaching inns, stables, warehouses, taverns, and mixed-use buildings line the principal roads, while quieter residential streets fill the spaces between them. Who Lives or Works Here: Cart drivers, stablehands, innkeepers, guards, messengers, ferrymen, and small merchants are common. Its central location also attracts residents who work elsewhere in the city.Purpose: The Eastgate serves as the main point of entry for travelers and goods arriving overland. It provides services for caravans before they enter the more crowded center of Zephyros. It also provides temporary housing for travelers coming from far away. Appearance: The district is less densely built than the rest of southern Zephyros. Large courtyards, stables, storage yards, workshops, warehouses, and roadside inns stand along the roads leading from its fortified entry gates. Who Lives or Works Here: Caravan merchants, animal handlers, guards, farmers, craftspeople, and travelers are common. Many residents make their living supplying or repairing wagons before they continue into or out of the city.Purpose:
The Gilded Quay hosts many affluent waterfront estates and mansions. Properties in the Gilded Quay are often reserved for members of the royal families, wealthy aristocrats, and foreign representatives. The ports in the Gilded Quay are private access for residents only The district also has one property reserved for the most recent winner of the Winterlow Trials. Appearance: Grand stone residences and ornate commercial buildings overlook private piers and landscaped courtyards. Intricate facades and alabaster sculptures decorate the carefully maintained streets. Who Lives or Works Here: Merchant families, diplomats, financiers, visiting dignitaries, and other wealthy residents live here. Their households employ servants, guards, interpreters, and specialist craftspeople.Purpose: The Hallowed Ward houses all of Zephyros' funerary service, such as cemeteries/burial grounds. Many houses of worship also have buildings in the district in close proximity to the burial grounds. Appearance: The district is quieter and more open than the surrounding wards. Temples, shrines, mausoleums, gardens, and tree-lined paths occupy much of its land, with residences and workshops concentrated along its outer roads. Who Lives or Works Here: Clergy, groundskeepers, healers, undertakers, scribes, and craftspeople who produce religious or funerary goods work here. Very few people permanently live in the Hallowed Ward, though visitors are common

campaigns/campaign-1/storylines/act-1/pl.title: Plot Point 1
campaigns/campaign-1/storylines/act-1/pl.description:
Recommended Level: 3Opener for Campaign 1.
Idea: Mathias Malnor, leader of the Alterations Department is set to be executed publicly, but the execution is not completed when the display is attacked and Malnor escapes. The breakout attempt creates chaos in the city center, as mercenaries attack from all sides. In the battle, players assist the city guards in taking down the mercenaries. After the area is cleared, an escort for a local Lord spots the players and brings them to Lord Balen Varros. Varros hires the players to form a group and assist in tracking down Malnor.
Location: The City of Zephyros
People: Mathias Malnor, Solvik, Balen Varros, Vox Winterlow
Groups: Alterations Department, Eye of Zephyros, Hand of Zephyros, Will of Zephyros
Mathias Malnor has been captured, tried, and sentenced to be put to death on display. News of the underground Alterations Department's activities in the city of Zephyros spreads fast. Much of the city, horrified by the department's actions, have gathered at the city center to spectate the execution. Campaign starts separated, following in player in what they do in the time leading up to the execution
The king of Zephyros, Vox Winterlow, addresses the crowd at the city center, detailing the crimes that Malnor committed. Right before the execution is completed, a series of explosions disrupts the scene and Malnor broken out. Masked figures surround city center and begin attacking into the crowd
Players, alongside the city guard and Solvik, fight off against the masked figures until they are eventually defeated. Solvik, spots the players assisting in defeating the masked figures and messages each of them to meet her in a nearby alley
The players meet each other for the first time, then they are introduced to Solvik, who mysteriously leads them to an isolated home in the High District. The home belongs to Balen Varros, the old lord who captured Malnor and turned him in.
The Alterations Department is a trafficking ring that has been running underground in Zephyros for decades, mostly staying hidden from the eyes of citizens and law enforcement alike. After losing his son, Pavren Varros, to the department, Lord Balen Varros set out to find and bring down the notorious ring. After 4 years of searching, Balen tracks down the group's leader, Mathias Malnor. Varros discovered that Malnor was searching for Nullstone, a rare magical crystal capable of separating a soul from the body. Varros managed to track Malnor's supplier, and thus Malnor. The two fight with Varros being the eventual victor. Balen Varros turns Malnor in to the authorities of Zephyros, alongside the evidence needed to warrant his execution. In their conflict, Malnor managed to injure Varros right before he was defeated, severing Varro's leg. Due to his lack of trust in the authority's competence when it comes to tracking Malnor, Varros sends his escort, Solvik, to attend the execution in his place, as his disability does not allow him the freedom to attend himself. The adventure is concluded once the party defeats Malnor. A public bounty will be placed on Malnor by the government, as well as a bounty placed by Lord Varros. If the players present information pertaining to Malnor's capture to law enforcement, they will be awarded by the city and lost Varros' favor. On the other hand, going to kill Malnor themselves would award the party favor to Varros, but they lose out on the greater bounty placed by the city.Placeholder

campaigns/campaign-1/z_home-rules/home-r.title: Home Rules
campaigns/campaign-1/z_home-rules/home-r.description:
Exotic weapon training (from Valda's) is unlocked on a weapon-by-weapon basis. If you have martial weapon training, you can use an exotic weapon (given you meet its requirements). Once you use the weapon (as your primary weapon) for a level up, you gain proficiency in that specific weapon. Until then, you do not add prof. bonus to attacks made with that weapon.
If you use a potion in combat, you may use your action to arcana check the potion. If roll is high enough, you use your bonus action to use the potion for max healing. No other actions may be done in that turn. Giving another player a potion requires an action
Help action for mental abilities (INT, WIS, and CHA) does not grant advantage. Instead, all involved players will rolls and add their individual rolls. Depending on what the check is for, the DC will get more challenging as more players use the help action
NAT20 on initiative roll lets you choose where you go on initative
Players who have the same initiative can combo their attacks. A combo attack must make logical sense and will use up the reactions of both players for that turn.

lore/pantheon/soul.html.title: Soul
lore/pantheon/soul.html.description:
Soul is the father of all creation in Drakensveil. Soul's being is split into four tempers, which in combination are used to provide souls to the living. The four tempers are Woe, Frolic, Dread, and Malice.
At the dawn of time, Soul harness the volatile energy in the Zero Plane to create 12 children split into 4 triads, each representing one of Soul's tempers.

drakensveil.html.title: Drakensveil
drakensveil.html.description: The Realm of Pursuit is a cosmic container for 12 material planes of existence, each acting as the physical domain for a single deity from the Eternal Ones. The 12 planes exist in a space known as the Zero Plane, an endless expanse of pure creation energy.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
